For each stochastic process (xt)t∈T(x_{t})_{t \in \mathrm{T}} we define the transition function as the law of xtx_{t} under the probability measure ℙx\mathbb{P}_{x}: ∀x∈X,∀K∈ℬX:Pt(x,K):=ℙx(xt∈K).\forall \,x \in \mathrm{X}, \quad \forall \,\mathrm{K}\in \mathcal{B}_\mathrm{X} \;:\quad \mathrm{P}_{t}(x, \mathrm{K}) \;:=\; \mathbb{P}_{x}(x_{t} \in \mathrm{K}).

Definition 40

A Markov process in X\mathrm{X} is a stochastic process (xt)t∈T(x_{t})_{t \in \mathrm{T}} adapted to the filtration ℱt\mathcal{F}_{t} and satisfying: ∀x∈X,∀K∈ℬX,∀t,s∈T:\forall \,x \in \mathrm{X}, \quad \forall \,\mathrm{K}\in \mathcal{B}_\mathrm{X}, \quad \forall \,t, s \in \mathrm{T}: ℙx(x0=x)=1andℙx-∀Ⅎω∈Ω:ℙx(xt+s∈K∣ℱs)=Pt(xs,K).\mathbb{P}_x(x_0\,=\,x) \,=\, 1 \qquad\mathrm{and}\qquad\mathbb{P}_x\,\text{-}\,\forall \hspace{-0.1em} \Finv\, \omega \in \Omega \;:\quad \mathbb{P}_x(x_{t + s}\in \mathrm{K}\mid \mathcal{F}_s) \,=\, \mathrm{P}_t(x_s, \mathrm{K}).

Remark

We denote "for μ\mu-almost every" as "μ-∀Ⅎ\mu\,\text{-}\,\forall \hspace{-0.1em} \Finv\,".

Definition 41

Given λ∈𝒫(X)\lambda \in \mathcal{P}(\mathrm{X}) and a Markov process (xt,ℙx)(x_{t}, \mathbb{P}_{x}), we define the probability measure ℙλ:ℱ→𝑹A↦∫Xℙx(A)λ(dx),\begin{array}{lccl} \mathbb{P}_{\lambda}: & \mathcal{F} & \longrightarrow & \mathbf{R}\\ & \mathrm{A} & \longmapsto & \displaystyle\int_{\mathrm{X}} \mathbb{P}_{x}(\mathrm{A}) \lambda(\mathrm{d}x), \end{array} and denote by 𝔼λ\mathbb{E}_{\lambda} the corresponding mean value.

Lemma 51 (Kolmogorov-Chapman)

∀x∈X,∀K∈ℬX,∀t,s∈T:\forall \,x \in \mathrm{X}, \quad \forall \,\mathrm{K}\in \mathcal{B}_\mathrm{X}, \quad \forall \,t, s \in \mathrm{T}: Pt+s(x,K)=∫XPt(x,dy)Ps(y,K).\mathrm{P}_{t+s}(x, \mathrm{K})\,=\,\int_{\mathrm{X}} \mathrm{P}_{t}(x, \mathrm{d}y) \mathrm{P}_{s}(y, \mathrm{K}).

Remark

This relation implies that every Markov process generates an evolution in the space of probability measures.

Proof.

We have Pt+s(x,K)=𝔼x𝟙K(xt+s)=𝔼x[𝔼x(𝟙K(xt+s)∣ℱt)]=𝔼xPs(xt,K)=∫XPt(x,dy)Ps(y,K)\begin{align*} \mathrm{P}_{t+s}(x, \mathrm{K}) \,=\, \mathbb{E}_{x} \mathbb{1}_{\mathrm{K}}(x_{t+s}) &\,=\, \mathbb{E}_{x}\left[\mathbb{E}_{x}(\mathbb{1}_{\mathrm{K}}(x_{t+s}) \mid \mathcal{F}_{t})\right] \\ &\,=\, \mathbb{E}_{x} \mathrm{P}_{s} (x_{t}, \mathrm{K}) \,=\, \int_{\mathrm{X}} \mathrm{P}_{t}(x, \mathrm{d}y) \mathrm{P}_{s}(y, \mathrm{K}) \end{align*} where we used the fact that the law of xtx_{t} under ℙx\mathbb{P}_{x} coincides with Pt(x,⋅)\mathrm{P}_{t}(x, \cdot). ◻

To each Markov process there correspond two families of linear operators acting in the spaces of bounded measurable functions L∞(X)\mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\mathrm{X}) and of probability measures 𝒫(X)\mathcal{P}(\mathrm{X}).

Definition 42

The transition operator Pt:L∞(X)→L∞(X)\mathrm{P}_{t}:\mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\mathrm{X})\longrightarrow\mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\mathrm{X}) of (xt)(x_t) is defined for all h∈L∞(X,𝑹)h \in \mathrm{L}^\infty(\mathrm{X},\mathbf{R}) by: Pth:X→𝑹x↦∫Xh(y)Pt(x,dy).\begin{array}{lccl} \mathrm{P}_{t} h: & \mathrm{X} & \longrightarrow & \mathbf{R}\\ & x & \longmapsto & \displaystyle\int_\mathrm{X}h(y) \mathrm{P}_{t}(x, \mathrm{d}y). \end{array}

Definition 43

The dual transition operator Pt*:𝒫(X)→𝒫(X)\mathrm{P}_{t}^\ast:\mathcal{P}(\mathrm{X})\longrightarrow\mathcal{P}(\mathrm{X}) of (xt)(x_t) is defined for all μ∈𝒫(X)\mu \in \mathcal{P}(\mathrm{X}) by: Pt*μ:ℬX→𝑹K↦∫XPt(x,K)dμ(x).\begin{array}{lccl} \mathrm{P}_{t}^\ast \mu: & \mathcal{B}_\mathrm{X} & \longrightarrow & \mathbf{R}\\ & \mathrm{K} & \longmapsto & \displaystyle\int_\mathrm{X}\mathrm{P}_{t}(x, \mathrm{K})\mathrm{d}\mu(x). \end{array}

Proposition 52 (Semigroup property)

These two operators are semigroups.

Proof.

Use the Kolmogorov-Chapman relation. ◻

Proposition 53 (Duality relation)

They satisfy the following relation: ∀f∈L∞(X),∀μ∈𝒫(X):⟨Ptf,μ⟩=⟨f,Pt*μ⟩.\forall \,f \in \mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\mathrm{X}), \quad \forall \,\mu \in \mathcal{P}(\mathrm{X}) \;:\quad \left\langle \mathrm{P}_{t} f, \mu \right\rangle\,=\, \left\langle f, \mathrm{P}_{t}^{\ast} \mu \right\rangle.

Proof.

Use the Fubini’s theorem. ◻

Proposition 54

The ℙλ\mathbb{P}_{\lambda}-law of xtx_{t} coincides with Pt*λ\mathrm{P}_{t}^{\ast} \lambda.

Corollary 55

∀f∈L∞(X):𝔼λf(xt)=∫XPtf(x)λ(dx).\forall \,f \in \mathrm{L}^{\infty}(\mathrm{X}) \;:\quad \mathbb{E}_{\lambda} f (x_{t}) \,=\, \int_{X} \mathrm{P}_{t} f(x) \lambda(\mathrm{d}x).

Definition 44

A measure μ∈𝒫(X)\mu \in \mathcal{P}(X) is said to be stationary for (xt,ℙx)(x_{t}, \mathbb{P}_{x}) if: ∀t∈T:Pt*μ=μ.\forall \,t \in \mathrm{T}\;:\quad \mathrm{P}_{t}^{\ast} \mu \,=\, \mu.

Appendix BNoncommutative algebra results

B.1. Exterior powers

Let E\mathrm{E} be a real vector space of dimension dd. For 1≤k≤d1 \,\leqslant\,k \,\leqslant\,d we consider the kk-fold exterior power of E\mathrm{E}, denoted ∧kE\wedge^{k} \mathrm{E}, be the vector space of alternating kk-linear forms on the dual space E*\mathrm{E}^{*}. We can identify this set with the set of formal expressions: ∑i=1mci(u1(i)∧…∧uk(i)),\sum_{i=1}^{m} c_{i}\left(u_{1}^{(i)} \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{k}^{(i)}\right), with m∈𝑵m \in \mathbf{N}, ci∈𝑹c_{i} \in \mathbf{R} and uj(i)∈Eu_{j}^{(i)} \in \mathrm{E} if we do computations with the following conventions:

  • u1∧…∧(uj+uj′)∧…∧uk=(u1∧…∧uj∧…∧uk)+(u1∧…∧uj′∧…∧uk)u_{1} \wedge \ldots \wedge\left(u_{j}+u_{j}^{\prime}\right) \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{k}\,=\,\left(u_{1} \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{j} \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{k}\right)+\left(u_{1} \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{j}^{\prime} \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{k}\right),

  • u1∧…∧cuj∧…∧uk=c(u1∧…∧uj∧…∧uk)u_{1} \wedge \ldots \wedge c u_{j} \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{k} \,=\,c\left(u_{1} \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{j} \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{k}\right),

  • ∀σ∈𝔖k:uσ(1)∧…∧uσ(k)=sign⁡(π)u1∧…∧uk\forall \,\sigma \in \mathfrak{S}_k\;:\quad u_{\sigma(1)} \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{\sigma(k)} \,=\, \operatorname{sign}(\pi) \, u_{1} \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{k}.

The elements in ∧kE\wedge^{k} E of the form u1∧…∧uku_{1} \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{k} are called decomposable kk vectors.

The following facts can be readily checked.

Lemma 56 (Exterior powers of spaces and operators)

Let (e1,…,ed)(e_{1}, \ldots, e_{d}) be a basis of E\mathrm{E}.

  • (ei1∧…∧eik)1≤i1<…<ik≤d(e_{i_{1}} \wedge \ldots \wedge e_{i_{k}})_{1 \,\leqslant\,i_{1}< \ldots <i_{k} \,\leqslant\,d} is a basis of ∧kE\wedge^{k} \mathrm{E}. In particular, dim⁡(∧kE)=(dk).\dim (\wedge^{k} \mathrm{E}) \,=\, \binom{d}{k}.

  • ∀(u1,…,uk):u1∧…∧uk=0⇔u1,…,uk\forall \,(u_1,\hdots,u_k) \;:\quad u_{1} \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{k}\,=\,0 \qquad \Longleftrightarrow\qquad u_{1}, \ldots, u_{k} are linearly dependent.

  • Two sets (u1,…,uk)(u_{1}, \ldots, u_{k}) and (v1,…,vk)(v_{1}, \ldots, v_{k}) of kk linearly independent vectors in E\mathrm{E} have the same linear span if and only if there exists λ∈𝑹\lambda \in \mathbf{R} such that: u1∧…∧uk=λ(v1∧…∧vk).u_{1} \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{k} \,=\, \lambda (v_{1} \wedge \ldots \wedge v_{k}).

  • If E\mathrm{E} has the scalar product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle, then the bilinear extension of ⟨u1∧⋯∧uk,v1∧⋯∧vk⟩:=det⁡(⟨ui,vj⟩)k×k,\left\langle u_{1} \wedge \cdots \wedge u_{k}, v_{1} \wedge \cdots \wedge v_{k} \right\rangle \;:=\; \det(\left\langle u_{i}, v_{j} \right\rangle)_{k \times k}, defines a scalar product in ∧kE\wedge^{k} \mathrm{E}. In particular, ∥u1∧⋯∧uk∥=det⁡(⟨ui,uj⟩)k×k\left\|u_{1} \wedge \cdots \wedge u_{k}\right\|_{} \,=\, \sqrt{\det(\left\langle u_{i}, u_{j} \right\rangle)_{k \times k}} is the volume of the kk-dimensional parallelepiped spanned by u1,…,uku_{1}, \ldots, u_{k}. Further, the generalized Hadamard’s inequality holds: For 1≤p<k1 \,\leqslant\,p\,<\,k: ∥u1∧⋯∧uk∥≤∥u1∧⋯∧up∥∥up+1∧⋯∧uk∥.\left\|u_{1} \wedge \cdots \wedge u_{k}\right\|_{} \,\leqslant\,\left\|u_{1} \wedge \cdots \wedge u_{p}\right\|_{} \left\|u_{p+1} \wedge \cdots \wedge u_{k}\right\|_{}.

  • If A:E→EA: \mathrm{E}\longrightarrow\mathrm{E} is a linear operator, then:

    • the linear extension of ∧kA(u1∧⋯∧uk):=Au1∧⋯∧Auk\wedge^{k} A(u_{1} \wedge \cdots \wedge u_{k}) \;:=\; A u_{1} \wedge \cdots \wedge A u_{k} defines a linear operator ∧kA\wedge^{k} A on ∧kE\wedge^{k} \mathrm{E}, the kk-fold exterior power of AA, with ∧1A=A,∧dA=det⁡Aand∧kI=I.\wedge^{1} A \,=\, A, \qquad \wedge^{d} A \,=\, \det A \qquad\mathrm{and}\qquad\wedge^{k} I \,=\, I.

    • ∧kA\wedge^{k}A has eigenvalues (λi1⋯λik)1≤i1<⋯<ik≤d(\lambda_{i_{1}} \cdots \lambda_{i_{k}})_{1 \,\leqslant\,i_{1}<\cdots<i_{k} \,\leqslant\,d}, where λ1,…,λd\lambda_{1}, \ldots, \lambda_{d} are the eigenvalues of AA,

    • for all BB: ∧k(AB)=(∧kA)(∧kB),(∧kA)−1=∧kA−1,∧k(cA)=ck∧kA,\wedge^{k}(A B)=(\wedge^{k} A)(\wedge^{k} B), \quad(\wedge^{k} A)^{-1} \,=\,\wedge^{k} A^{-1}, \quad \wedge^{k}(c A)=c^{k} \wedge^{k} A,

    • det⁡(∧kA)=(det⁡A)(d−1k−1)\displaystyle\det(\wedge^{k} A) \,=\, (\det A)^{\binom{d-1}{k-1}},

    • If AA is an upper/lower triangular matrix in some basis then so is ∧kA\wedge^{k} A in the corresponding basis of (i).

  • Let EE have a scalar product and let ∧kE\wedge^{k} E be endowed with the scalar product introduced in part (iv). If UU is orthogonal, then ∧kU\wedge^{k} U is orthogonal. Further, ⟨∧kA(u1∧…∧uk),v1∧…∧vk⟩=det⁡(⟨Aui,vj⟩)k×k,\left\langle \wedge^{k} A (u_{1} \wedge \ldots \wedge u_{k}), v_{1} \wedge \ldots \wedge v_{k} \right\rangle \,=\, \det(\left\langle A u_{i}, v_{j} \right\rangle)_{k \times k}, hence, with ∥∧kA∥\left\|\wedge^{k} A\right\|_{} denoting the corresponding operator norm, ∥∧k(AB)∥≤∥∧kA∥∥∧kB∥and(∧kA)*=∧kA*.\left\|\wedge^{k}(A B)\right\|_{} \,\leqslant\,\left\|\wedge^{k} A\right\|_{}\left\|\wedge^{k} B\right\|_{} \qquad\mathrm{and}\qquad(\wedge^{k} A)^{\ast} \,=\, \wedge^{k} A^{\ast}.

Lemma 57 (Singular values of exterior power)

Let A∈ℳd(𝑹)A\in\mathcal{M}_d(\mathbf{R}), let A=VDUA \,=\, V D U be a singular value decomposition and let σ1≥…≥σd≥0\sigma_{1} \,\geqslant\,\ldots \,\geqslant\,\sigma_{d} \,\geqslant\,0 be the singular values of AA. Then:

  • a singular value decomposition of ∧kA\wedge^{k} A is: ∧kA=(∧kV)(∧kD)(∧kU).\wedge^{k} A \,=\, (\wedge^{k} V)(\wedge^{k} D)(\wedge^{k} U).

  • for k∈⟦1,d⟧:k\in\llbracket 1,d \rrbracket:

    • ∧kD=Diag(σi1⋯σik,1≤i1<…<ik≤d)\wedge^{k} D \,=\, \text{Diag}(\sigma_{i_{1}} \cdots \sigma_{i_{k}}, \; 1 \,\leqslant\,i_{1}<\ldots<i_{k} \,\leqslant\,d),

    • the top singular value of ∧kA\wedge^{k} A is σ1⋯σk\sigma_{1} \cdots \sigma_{k},

    • the smallest is σd−k+1⋯σd\sigma_{d-k+1} \cdots \sigma_{d}.

    Moreover, if AA is positive-definite (semi-definite) then so is ∧kA\wedge^{k} A.

  • for all 1≤k,m,k+m≤d:1 \,\leqslant\,k, m, k+m \,\leqslant\,d \;:

    • ∥∧kA∥=σ1⋯σkand∥∧dA∥=σ1⋯σd=|det⁡A|\left\|\wedge^{k} A\right\|_{} \,=\, \sigma_{1} \cdots \sigma_{k} \qquad\mathrm{and}\qquad\left\|\wedge^{d} A\right\|_{} \,=\, \sigma_{1} \cdots \sigma_{d} \,=\, |\det A|,

    • ∥∧k+mA∥≤∥∧kA∥∥∧mA∥\left\|\wedge^{k+m} A\right\|_{} \,\leqslant\,\left\|\wedge^{k} A\right\|_{} \left\|\wedge^{m} A\right\|_{},

    • ∥∧kA∥≤∥A∥k\left\|\wedge^{k} A\right\|_{} \,\leqslant\,\left\|A\right\|_{}^{k},

    where ∥⋅∥\left\|\cdot\right\|_{} is the operator norm associated with the standard Euclidean norm in 𝑹d\mathbf{R}^{d}.

B.2. Proof of Baxendale-Furstenberg lemma

  • First point: assume that H\mathrm{H} is a compact subgroup of SLd(𝑹)\mathrm{S}\mathrm{L}_{d}(\mathbf{R}).

By compacity, H\mathrm{H} admits a right-invariant Haar probability measure γ\gamma, that is: γ\gamma is a Borel probability measure on H\mathrm{H} such that ∀A∈H,∀K∈ℬH:γ(KA)=γ(K).\forall \,A \in \mathrm{H}, \quad \forall \,K \in \mathcal{B}_\mathrm{H}\;:\quad \gamma(K A) \,=\, \gamma(K). Hence, we define ⟨⋅,⋅⟩′\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle^{\prime} on 𝑹d\mathbf{R}^{d} by: ∀u,v∈𝑹d:⟨u,v⟩′:=∫H(Au,Av)γ(dA),\forall \,u, v \in \mathbf{R}^{d} \;:\quad \left\langle u, v \right\rangle^{\prime} \;:=\; \int_{\mathrm{H}}(A u, A v) \, \gamma(\mathrm{d}A), where (⋅,⋅)(\cdot, \cdot) the standard inner product on 𝑹d\mathbf{R}^{d}. Using right-invariance of γ\gamma, we have that ∀u,v∈𝑹d,∀A∈H:⟨Au,Av⟩′=⟨u,v⟩′.\forall \,u, v \in \mathbf{R}^{d}, \quad \forall \,A \in \mathrm{H}\;:\quad \left\langle A u, A v \right\rangle^{\prime} \,=\, \left\langle u, v \right\rangle^{\prime}.

  • Second point: assume that H\mathrm{H} is a non-compact.

Let us first state and prove the following useful lemma.

Lemma 58

Let k≥1k \,\geqslant\,1 and let (Mn)n∈SLk(𝑹)(M_{n})_n\in\mathrm{S}\mathrm{L}_k(\mathbf{R}) such that ∥Mn∥→n+∞∞.\left\|M_{n}\right\|_{} \;\;\xrightarrow[n+\infty]{}\;\; \infty. Then, on refining to a subsequence (Mφ(n))n(M_{\varphi(n)})_n, there exist proper linear subspaces V1,V2⊂𝑹k\mathrm{V}_{1}, \mathrm{V}_{2} \subset \mathbf{R}^{k} for which ∀v∉V1:d(Mφ(n)v,V2)→n+∞0.\forall \,v \notin \mathrm{V}_{1} \;:\quad \mathrm{d}(M_{\varphi(n)} v, \mathrm{V}_{2}) \;\;\xrightarrow[n+\infty]{}\;\; 0.

Proof.

Using the fact that det⁡(Mn)=1\det (M_{n}) \,=\, 1 for all nn, we can, without loss, pass to a subsequence with the property that for some fixed 1≤ℓ<k1 \,\leqslant\,\ell \,<\,k, we have σℓ(Mn)σℓ+1(Mn)→n+∞+∞.(*)\frac{\sigma_{\ell}(M_{n})}{\sigma_{\ell+1}(M_{n})} \;\;\xrightarrow[n+\infty]{}\;\; +\infty. \qquad (\ast) Applying the Singular Value Decomposition to each MnM_{n}:

  • let V1n\mathrm{V}^{n}_{1} be the unique (k−ℓ)(k-\ell)-dimensional subspace for which: ∥Mn∥V1n=σℓ+1(Mn)\left\|M_{n}\right\|_{\mathrm{V}^{n}_{1}} \,=\, \sigma_{\ell+1}(M_{n}),

  • let V2n\mathrm{V}^{n}_{2} be the unique ℓ\ell-dimensional subspace for which: ∥Mn−1∥V2n=(σℓ(Mn))−1\left\|M_{n}^{-1}\right\|_{\mathrm{V}^{n}_{2}} \,=\, (\sigma_{\ell}(M_{n}))^{-1}.

Passing to a further subsequence, we can assume that the subspaces V1n,V2n\mathrm{V}^{n}_{1}, \mathrm{V}^{n}_{2} converge to subspaces V1,V2\mathrm{V}_{1}, \mathrm{V}_{2}, respectively. The result now follows from (*)(\ast). ◻

Now, consider the set 𝒢\mathcal{G} of finite tuples of proper, nontrivial, distinct subspaces (E1,…,Ep)(\mathrm{E}^1,\hdots,\mathrm{E}^p) of 𝑹d\mathbf{R}^{d} for which η(⋃i=1pEi)=1.\eta\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^p \mathrm{E}^{i}\right) \,=\, 1. Applying the previous lemma to a sequence (Mn)∈H𝑵(M_{n}) \in \mathrm{H}^\mathbf{N} with ∥Mn∥→∞\left\|M_{n}\right\|_{} \longrightarrow\infty, note that the pair (V1,V2)(\mathrm{V}_1, \mathrm{V}_2) so-obtained is such a tuple. If (E1,…,Ep)(\mathrm{E}_1,\hdots,\mathrm{E}_p), (F1,…,Fq)(\mathrm{F}_1,\hdots,\mathrm{F}_q) are two such tuples, let us write: (Ei)≤(Fi)⇔⋃iEi⊂⋃iFi.(\mathrm{E}^{i}) \,\leqslant\,(\mathrm{F}^{i}) \qquad \Longleftrightarrow\qquad \bigcup_{i} \mathrm{E}_{i} \;\subset\; \bigcup_{i} \mathrm{F}_{i}. Note that ≤\,\leqslant\, is a partial order on 𝒢\mathcal{G}. We say that two tuples (E1,…,Ep)(\mathrm{E}_1,\hdots,\mathrm{E}_p), (F1,…,Fq)(\mathrm{F}_1,\hdots,\mathrm{F}_q) in 𝒢\mathcal{G} are equivalent up to relabeling if: p=qand∃π∈𝔖p:∀j∈⟦1,p⟧:Fj=Eπ(j).p\,=\,q \qquad\mathrm{and}\qquad\exists \,\pi\in\mathfrak{S}_p \;:\quad \forall \,j \in \llbracket 1,p \rrbracket \;:\quad \mathrm{F}^{j}\,=\,\mathrm{E}^{\pi(j)}. Let us state and prove a series of Lemmas which the second point.

Lemma 59

There is a unique tuple (E1,…,Ep)(\mathrm{E}_1,\hdots,\mathrm{E}_p) (up to relabeling) of distinct, proper and nontrivial linear subspaces of 𝑹d\mathbf{R}^{d} minimal with respect to the partial order ≤\,\leqslant\, on 𝒢\mathcal{G}, and such that: ∀A∈Hη,∃π=πA∈𝔖p,∀i∈⟦1,p⟧:AEi=Eπ(i).\forall \,A \in \mathrm{H}_{\eta}, \quad \exists \,\pi\,=\,\pi_{A} \in \mathfrak{S}_p, \quad \forall \,i\in\llbracket 1,p \rrbracket \;:\quad A \mathrm{E}^{i} \,=\, \mathrm{E}^{\pi(i)}.

Proof.

Straightforward. ◻

The minimal tuple (Ei)(E^{i}) therefore satisfies conditions (i)(i)-(ii)(ii) in the Lemma 41. Item (iii)(iii) is verified below.

Lemma 60

For each i∈⟦1,p⟧i \in \llbracket 1,p \rrbracket, there is an inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩i\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle^{i} on Ei\mathrm{E}^{i} such that: ∀A∈H:A:(Ei,⟨⋅,⋅⟩i)→(Eπ(i),⟨⋅,⋅⟩π(i)))is a conformal mapping,\forall \,A \in \mathrm{H}\;:\quad A : (\mathrm{E}^{i},\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle^{i}) \;\longrightarrow\; (\mathrm{E}^{\pi(i)},\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle^{\pi(i))}) \;\;\text{is a conformal mapping}, where π=πA∈𝔖p\pi \,=\, \pi_{A}\in\mathfrak{S}_p.

Proof.

We denote H̃⊂H\widetilde{\mathrm{H}} \subset \mathrm{H} a closed, normal subgroup of finite index H̃=H̃η={A∈Hη:AEi=Ei}.\widetilde{\mathrm{H}} \,=\, \widetilde{\mathrm{H}}_{\eta} \,=\, \left\{A \in \mathrm{H}_{\eta} \;:\; A \mathrm{E}^{i} \,=\, \mathrm{E}^{i}\right\}. The quotient group H/H̃\mathrm{H}/\widetilde{\mathrm{H}} is naturally isomorphic to a subgroup of 𝔖p\mathfrak{S}_p.
Let us assume for the moment that 𝔖p\mathfrak{S}_p acts transitively on ⟦1,p⟧\llbracket 1,p \rrbracket. Fix an arbitrary i∈⟦1,p⟧i \in \llbracket 1,p \rrbracket and form Ȟ(i)={det(A|Ei)−1dim⁡(Ei)A|Ei,A∈H̃}.\check{\mathrm{H}}^{(i)} \,=\, \left\{\det\left(A_{\vert\mathrm{E}^{i}}\right)^{-\frac{1}{\dim(\mathrm{E}^{i})}} A_{\vert \mathrm{E}^{i}}, \; A \in \widetilde{\mathrm{H}}\right\}. Note that linear operators in Ȟ(i)\check{\mathrm{H}}^{(i)} preserve the measure η|Ei\eta_{\vert \mathrm{E}^{i}}. Since any A∈H̃A \in \widetilde{\mathrm{H}} maps Ei\mathrm{E}^{i} into itself, we can think of Ȟ(i)\check{\mathrm{H}}^{(i)} as a subgroup of SLdim⁡Ei(𝑹)\mathrm{S}\mathrm{L}_{\dim\mathrm{E}^{i}}(\mathbf{R}) on identifying Ei\mathrm{E}^{i} with 𝑹dim⁡Ei\mathbf{R}^{\dim\mathrm{E}^{i}}.

  • We have that Ȟ(i)\check{\mathrm{H}}^{(i)} is compact. Indeed, if it is not compact, then by Lemma 58 there are proper linear subspaces W1,W2⊂Ei\mathrm{W}^{1}, \mathrm{W}^{2} \subset \mathrm{E}^{i} for which η(W1∪W2)=η(Ei)\eta\left(\mathrm{W}^{1} \cup \mathrm{W}^{2}\right) \,=\, \eta(\mathrm{E}^{i}). This contradicts minimality of (E1,…,Ep)(\mathrm{E}_1,\hdots,\mathrm{E}_p) as in item (i)(i).

  • It now follows from (a)(a) that there exists an inner product ⟨⋅,⋅⟩i\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle^{i} on Ei\mathrm{E}^{i} with respect to which Ȟ(i)\check{\mathrm{H}}^{(i)} acts isometrically. Equivalently, linear operators of the form A|Ei,A∈H̃A_{\vert\mathrm{E}^{i}}, A \in \widetilde{\mathrm{H}} act conformally with respect to ⟨⋅,⋅⟩i\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle^{i}.

  • Since 𝔖p=H/H̃\mathfrak{S}_p \,=\, \mathrm{H}/\widetilde{\mathrm{H}} acts transitively on ⟦1,p⟧\llbracket 1, p \rrbracket: ∀j∈⟦1,p⟧,j≠i,∃M∈H:MEi=Ej\forall \,j\in\llbracket 1,p \rrbracket, \; j \neq i, \quad \exists \,M \in \mathrm{H}\;:\quad M \mathrm{E}^{i} \,=\, \mathrm{E}^{j} and we define ⟨⋅,⋅⟩j\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle^{j} as: ∀v,w∈Ej:⟨v,w⟩j=⟨M−1v,M−1w⟩i.\forall \,v, w \in \mathrm{E}^{j} \;:\quad \left\langle v, w \right\rangle^{j} \,=\, \left\langle M^{-1} v, M^{-1} w \right\rangle^{i}.

  • This definition is independent of MM : if NEi=EjN \mathrm{E}^{i}\,=\,\mathrm{E}^{j} for some other N∈HN \in \mathrm{H}, then ∀v,w∈Ej:⟨N−1v,N−1w⟩i=⟨M−1v,M−1w⟩i=⟨v,w⟩j.\forall \,v, w \in \mathrm{E}^{j} \;:\quad \left\langle N^{-1} v, N^{-1} w \right\rangle^{i}\,=\, \left\langle M^{-1} v, M^{-1} w \right\rangle^{i} \,=\, \left\langle v, w \right\rangle^{j}. By a similar computation, one checks that if A∈HA \in \mathrm{H} maps AEi=EjA \mathrm{E}^{i}\,=\,\mathrm{E}^{j}, then AA is conformal with respect to the inner products ⟨⋅,⋅⟩i,⟨⋅,⋅⟩j\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle^{i}, \left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle^{j}, respectively.

This completes the proof when 𝔖≅H/H̃\mathfrak{S}\cong \mathrm{H}/\widetilde{\mathrm{H}} acts transitively on ⟦1,p⟧\llbracket 1, p \rrbracket.
Let us now address the situation when 𝔖p\mathfrak{S}_p does not act transitively on ⟦1,p⟧\llbracket 1,p \rrbracket.

  • By a standard argument there is a unique partition (𝒫l)1≤l≤k(\mathcal{P}_{l})_{1 \,\leqslant\,l \,\leqslant\,k} of ⟦1,p⟧\llbracket 1,p \rrbracket, such that: 𝔖p𝒫l=𝒫l,and𝔖pacts transitively on 𝒫l.\mathfrak{S}_p \mathcal{P}_{l} \,=\, \mathcal{P}_{l}, \qquad\mathrm{and}\qquad\mathfrak{S}_p \;\;\text{acts transitively on }\; \mathcal{P}_{l}.

  • For each 𝒫l\mathcal{P}_{l}, repeat the construction of ⟨⋅,⋅⟩i\left\langle \cdot, \cdot \right\rangle^{i} for some fixed arbitrary i∈𝒫li \in \mathcal{P}_{l}, and then define ⟨⋅,⋅⟩j,j∈𝒫l,j≠i\langle\cdot, \cdot\rangle^{j}, j \in \mathcal{P}_{l}, j \neq i as in previously for some arbitrary M∈HM \in H sending MEi=EjM \mathrm{E}^{i}\,=\,\mathrm{E}^{j} (such an MM exists since 𝔖\mathfrak{S} acts transitively on 𝒫l\mathcal{P}_{l} by construction).

  • The result now follows from the previous arguments, since for all A∈HA \in H, we can have AEi=EjA \mathrm{E}^{i}\,=\,\mathrm{E}^{j} only if i,ji, j belong to the same 𝒫l\mathcal{P}_{l} for some 1≤l≤k1 \,\leqslant\,l \,\leqslant\,k.
